chunk_findings.detail: `ns.limit = a.limit or R.SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT` treats an explicitly supplied `--limit 0` as “not supplied” because `0` is falsy. For input `ddflow list search --query foo --limit 0`, this line replaces the requested limit with `R.SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT`, so the command silently ignores the user’s limit. The session branch below correctly preserves a present `0` and only defaults when the value is `None`; the search branch should do the same.
chunk_findings.title: viewers_lists.py:_other_viewer (search branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test uses `--query zzzz`, which is a no-match query. The buggy expression `a.limit or R.SEARCH_DEFAULT_LIMIT` changes behavior only when the search has more than the requested `--limit 0` results; with no matches, both the buggy and fixed code produce the same return code and stdout, so `assert a[:2] == b[:2]` would pass even on the unfixed code and never detects the regression. It should use a query with at least one hit and assert that `--limit 0` returns `total > 0` with zero rows / `truncated` reflecting the zero limit.
